In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the parallel transport of a connection in a principal fiber bundle, the holonomy operator and, as an application, the Gauss law constraint in Yang–Mills theory.
a new approach to the study of the parallel transport equation and holonomy operator in YM theories.
the study of the parallel propagators and holonomy operators of YM connections and their variations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Gauss law is a Hamiltonian constraint.
the variation of the holonomy operator is the solution of the parallel transport equation, where the connection is varied.
any congruence in a YM theory, with or without matter, defines a solution of its quantum Gauss law constraint.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
any curve in a YM connection defines a solution to the Gauss law constraints.
any solution of the Hamiltonian Gauss law constraint can be obtained from a solution of the Dirac Gauss law constraint.
the Gauss law constraint can be viewed as the equation for the variation of a parallel propagator.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Gauss law constraint in YM theories can be solved in the same way that a Hamilton–Jacobi equation is solved in classical mechanics.
the Gauss law constraint is the equation of motion for the holonomy operator of a Yang–Mills theory.
the Gauss law constraint, as it is usually written in terms of functional derivatives, is not the most general form of the Gauss law.
